overallAssessment.verdict: data/regions/wye-valley.ts is a well-structured location data file with hero copy, key facts, seasonal guide, insider tips, top experiences, FAQs, and hidden gems. Unlike some other region files, it does not explicitly cite AI research in its header, but it lists NO sources at all (just 'Last updated: February 2025'). This absence of provenance means all factual and pricing claims must be treated as unverified. Several specific claims (the River Wye length at '154 miles', the '50+ navigable miles' figure, the Wye Valley Walk endpoint description) are questionable against standard geographical references and need fact-checking. All pricing figures lack source URLs. The hero image exists on disk but has no provenance record; no OG/social image is defined anywhere in the TS data.
overallAssessment.structuralQuality: HIGH — the TS data file is well-organised with all required sections and good editorial voice. Suitable as the canonical source once claims are verified.
overallAssessment.factualConfidence: MEDIUM — geographic, heritage, and AONB designation facts are broadly consistent with standard references; the 154-mile River Wye length claim and navigable-miles figure are suspect; all pricing figures are unverified and carry no source URLs

verified_or_stable.claim: Wye Valley AONB — Designated 1971, shared with England
verified_or_stable.note: The Wye Valley Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty was designated in 1971. It straddles Monmouthshire (Wales) and Herefordshire/Gloucestershire (England). The AONB is managed by the Wye Valley AONB Partnership.

verified_or_stable.claim: Wye Valley Walk — 136 miles, from Plynlimon to Chepstow
verified_or_stable.note: The Wye Valley Walk is officially 136 miles (218 km). It runs from Chepstow northwards to Plynlimon in Powys. The TS data says 'Plynlimon to Chepstow' which describes the same route in reverse — the direction is not wrong, just reversed. The 136-mile figure is correct.

verified_or_stable.claim: Tintern Abbey — Cistercian foundation, ruined Gothic church
verified_or_stable.note: Tintern Abbey was founded in 1131 by Walter de Clare for the Cistercian order — the second Cistercian abbey in Britain. The current standing ruins are largely from the late 13th-century rebuilding. The description '12th-century Cistercian ruins' is an acceptable shorthand (founded 12th century; significant 13th-century rebuilding). Managed by Cadw.

verified_or_stable.claim: Forest of Dean — ancient woodland, approximately 42 sq miles
verified_or_stable.note: The Forest of Dean covers approximately 110 sq km (42 sq miles). This is consistent with Forestry England published area data.

verified_or_stable.claim: Symonds Yat Rock — one of UK's best peregrine falcon viewing spots
verified_or_stable.note: Symonds Yat Rock has hosted one of the UK's most accessible nesting peregrine sites since 1982. RSPB volunteers man telescopes during the nesting season (April–August). Well-documented and consistent across official sources.

verified_or_stable.claim: Chepstow and Monmouth — market towns with castle ruins
verified_or_stable.note: Chepstow Castle is a genuine Norman castle managed by Cadw. Monmouth Castle is also a Cadw-managed ruin. Both are in Monmouthshire, Wales.

verified_or_stable.claim: Hay Festival — listed under summer highlights
verified_or_stable.note: The Hay Festival of Literature & Arts is a real annual event in Hay-on-Wye, well-established since 1988. HOWEVER: the Festival typically runs in late May to early June — this falls in the spring/early-summer boundary and not squarely in the June–August 'summer' window as defined in the season guide. The Festival dates should be checked each year. In recent years it has run late May to early June. Listing it under the June–August summer section may mislead visitors who arrive in July expecting it.

verified_or_stable.claim: Clearwell Caves — limestone caves, Forest of Dean
verified_or_stable.note: Clearwell Caves is a genuine open-to-the-public show cave in the Forest of Dean, with a history of iron ore mining and natural cave systems. Real and operating.

Puzzlewood is a real ancient woodland site in the Forest of Dean, open to visitors. It has been used as a filming location for Doctor Who and reportedly as inspiration for J.R.R. Tolkien's Middle-earth (though the direct Tolkien link is disputed). The Star Wars location claim in the TS file (hiddenGems) specifically names Star Wars — this needs verification; Puzzlewood was used as a location for Star Wars: The Force Awakens scouting but the Millennium Falcon scene was filmed in Abu Dhabi. The Doctor Who link is confirmed. Recommend wording as 'used as a filming location for TV productions including Doctor Who' rather than specifically naming Star Wars.

verified_or_stable.claim: Devil's Pulpit — limestone viewpoint above Tintern Abbey
verified_or_stable.note: Devil's Pulpit is a genuine limestone outcrop on Offa's Dyke Path above Tintern offering views down to the abbey. The legend about the devil preaching to the monks is well-documented local tradition.

verified_or_stable.claim: River Wye straddles the Wales/England border
verified_or_stable.note: The River Wye forms much of the border between Wales (Monmouthshire) and England (Herefordshire, Gloucestershire) in its lower reaches. Tintern is in Wales (Monmouthshire). Symonds Yat Rock and the Forest of Dean are in England (Herefordshire/Gloucestershire). The FAQ answer in the TS file accurately reflects this cross-border character.

verified_or_stable.claim: Wintour's Leap — limestone climbing crag above the Wye
verified_or_stable.note: Wintour's Leap is a genuine limestone cliff near Chepstow on the English side of the Wye, a well-established trad and sport climbing area. Named after Colonel John Wintour who reportedly leapt his horse from the cliff to escape Roundheads.

verified_or_stable.claim: Pedalabikeaway — bike hire in Forest of Dean with trail maps
verified_or_stable.note: Pedalabikeaway is a real bike hire company operating in the Forest of Dean. Verify current trading status and pricing before publishing. The Cannop Cycles / Pedalabikeaway presence in the Forest is well-established.

verified_or_stable.claim: The Boat Inn at Penallt — riverside pub, canoe-friendly
verified_or_stable.note: A riverside pub at Penallt associated with the Wye Valley paddling community is well-known. The pub name as 'The Boat Inn' should be verified — it may now trade as 'The Inn at Penallt' or similar. Verify current trading status.

verified_or_stable.claim: Wye Valley Canoes — canoe hire with car shuttles
verified_or_stable.note: Wye Valley Canoes is a real canoe hire company on the River Wye. Appears in the content inventory as an operator (operator-wye-valley-canoes). Verify current trading status.

verified_or_stable.claim: Wye navigable Grade 1-2, suitable for beginners with basic instruction
verified_or_stable.note: The main paddled section of the Wye (Hay-on-Wye to Chepstow) is generally characterised as Grade 1–2 (moving water, no significant rapids) appropriate for beginners with basic instruction. Consistent with Canoe Wales guidance. Verify against current Canoe Wales information as conditions can vary.

crossBorderChallenge.issue: A significant proportion of the Wye Valley's most famous attractions are in England, not Wales

The FAQ ('Is the Wye Valley in Wales or England? Both—') handles this correctly but the overall page framing should be clear that the AONB is a cross-border area.

recommendedNextStatusRationale: The data/regions/wye-valley.ts file provides a solid structural and editorial foundation that accurately captures the region's character. The geographic, heritage, and AONB designation facts are broadly sound. However three issues must be resolved before the page is publishable: (1) the River Wye length claim of '154 miles' is likely incorrect (standard sources say ~134 miles) and must be verified before the page carries this prominent keyFact; (2) the hero image has no provenance record and cannot be published without legal clearance; (3) all pricing claims are unsourced and several are potentially stale. The lack of an OG image at all (not just a missing file but no field defined) is a fourth production-blocking issue. Once these are addressed and pricing spot-checked against named operators, the page warrants a QA pass.

blockers.detail: Four priceRange fields in topExperiences have no named operators and no source URLs: canoe hire (£50-80/day), Tintern Abbey admission (£9), Forest of Dean bike hire (£25-40), and rock climbing guide fees (£80-120). Tintern Abbey admission is a Cadw price that changes annually. The canoe and bike hire figures have no operator context. Incorrect pricing claims are a common source of visitor frustration and operator complaints on directory and location pages.
blockers.resolution: Human QA reviewer should verify each price against the operator's current website: Wye Valley Canoes (https://www.wyevalleycanoes.co.uk/) for canoe hire; Cadw (https://cadw.gov.wales/visit/places-to-visit/tintern-abbey) for abbey admission; Pedalabikeaway (https://www.pedalabikeaway.com/) for bike hire. The fastest safe path is to remove all price figures from the location landing page and push them to operator profile pages (which carry operator-sourced pricing) — a convention used on some other Adventure Wales location pages.
